utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Defence would like to raise a matter. Mr. Lukic. Oh, Mr. Stojanovic. Yes. It is about yesterday's witness, I do understand. Yes. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honours. Good morning. With your leave, just a few remarks. Yesterday evening, we received a statement from the Prosecution by mail. It is directly connected with yesterday's witness testimony and the possibility to reach a correct decision about the video-clip that was used during the witness's testimony yesterday. You're talking about a fact that the chain of custody of the original video-clip is directly in contradiction with what we heard yesterday and directly in contradiction with what we heard yesterday about the author of that video-clip. Yesterday we heard a testimony from which it arises that the -- that the person whose statement we received yesterday was actually the author of that part of clip that we saw yesterday. We would like to express our serious concern that a document of that nature had not been submitted to us at least sometime before the witness arrived in the court, and in that sense our suggestion would be that the witness, whom we heard yesterday, should be re-called because we would like to put to him what we have learned and what we arrived at after reading his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the Chamber is -- is quite willing to understand what you're referring to, but if you do not make us acquainted with the material you received, then, of course, we cannot follow you. There seems to be a -- Mr. Mladic seems not to receive the audio.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, I can be more specific. With your leave. Yesterday evening, we received a statement by a man. That man provided the statement to the investigators of the Tribunal on the 27th of November, 2002. In that statement, he describes the same event about the witness -- about which the witness testified yesterday. His testimony is directly in contradiction with yesterday's testimony. However, this would not be surprising if we didn't have a bench-mark in your decision about the admission of this video-clip. In that statement, that witness -- in the statement that we received yesterday, that witness says that he is the author of that video-clip, that he was an authorised official, he was a member of the police force who was sent to carry out an on-site investigation together with the Serbian police, and as a result he recorded that video-clip as a result of that investigation. And, finally, the witness also speaks about the chain of custody of this video-clip. He says that the original video-clip was in his hands, that a copy was made, and that on the following day that copy was sent to the CNN and the BBC. And according to what he knows, a day after that event was sent to those two broadcasting agencies, through the channels unknown to him, and that had a direct impact on the break in the negotiations that had started in Lisbon. Bearing in mind the contents of the statement, Your Honours, we believe that it would be fair to provide the Defence additional time for preparations and for the re-examination of the witness about the circumstances of the event. We would like to challenge what he said in his testimony yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Still, you are summarising and apparently the Chamber is invited to act on the basis of the content of a document which is still not known to it, apart from your summary. Before we continue, Prosecution, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone. We did provide the Defence with this witness statement. The video that we received, the footage we received, was obtained on the 30th of September, 2002. Subsequently, the individual who provided this video was interviewed and a witness statement was produced. The witness statement addresses the video that was taken. He states in the statement that most of the footage was taken by him and then sets out -- tracks the chain of custody and how the video eventually made it into the hands of the OTP. It is probably best at this stage, or from our perspective, to maybe deal with this in written submissions so that Your Honours will have a fuller understanding of who this individual is and what the information we have is and whether it's necessary to re-call the witness and on what basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I take it that -- no. The witness, of course, never travelled to The Hague so that's -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber invites the parties to make written submissions and provide the Chamber with the statement taken from the person who provided this video. I think the most logical way of dealing with the matter would be that, Mr. Stojanovic, you have now received the statement. You have developed some thoughts about it, that you start making submissions, and that -- then the Defence response, I take it that your request would be to deny admission?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honours. However, our concern - and with your leave, we will include it in our submission - our concern is that we received the statement after this testimony of the witness. If that statement had been disclosed to us any time before the arrival of this witness, it would be fair if we had been told that. However, we have no knowledge of that. Our cross-examination would have been different, had we known that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was the statement disclosed at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: My understanding is we just, in fact, found the statement yesterday and immediately handed it over to the Defence at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it was not previously disclosed. Could you make your written submissions within a week? Is that reasonable, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then after receipt of the Defence submission, on from the date when it's filed, the Prosecution is invited to respond within a week. No further preliminary matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I just may be excused now that this matter has been dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have a few matters which we could deal with at least -- no. Yes, the first one is the Defence was asked to make submissions on MFI'd Exhibits P186, P188, up to and including P190 and P192, by midday, Tuesday, the 25th of September. Yesterday, Mr. Lukic, when we raised this matter, you said you would -- after the break, address the matter, but -- well, it's still after the break, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour. I just want to say that, as you know, Your Honours, we filed our submission in written form on 17th of September on this issue, and we have nothing to add to this submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll look at your written submissions and -- thank you for that. One small matter. Mr. Lukic, I think you yesterday referred to the time - and perhaps, meanwhile, the witness could be brought into the courtroom - you referred to your estimate of seven hours for cross-examination, but that was adjusted later to five hours. And since I think you used up to -- close to two hours, one hour and 40 minutes, I think, you are encouraged to try to finish your cross-examination today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Selak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. And I also would like to remind you that you should not start answering until after a short pause, a pause between question and answer, and Mr. Lukic will do the same. And, finally, listen carefully to the question. If someone asks you, for example, did A come by car, then the answer is yes or no. Or he came by train. But there's no need to describe the car. It was a two-litre red car. That's not -- if someone is interested in the colour of the car, they'll ask you. Is that clear to you? So try to focus your answers on what has been asked. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Once again, good morning, Colonel Selak.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 09041.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We already saw it yesterday. You will remember, Colonel, the document is dated 14 April 1992. It was sent by the command of the 5th Corps. We already discussed that document, and we were reading from page 2 in B/C/S and in English, paragraph 1, where it is insisted that unity of the army force should be maintained. Do you remember whether at that time there were efforts made in order to have the JNA united; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We also discussed paragraph 5, where it says that military personnel should not be captured. You spoke about instances when military personnel was captured and their apartments confiscated. And finally page 3, paragraph 11, it says --

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that question. Bear with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It says organise the monitoring of the enemy which shows that there were constant attacks on the JNA, and it is well known who the enemy was. Let me ask you this: Is it correct that you yourself, on the 9th of April, 1992, reported to Colonel Kelecevic while you were in Jajce that there would be attack on the fuel storage in Jajce; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that because I was afraid that there would be consequences for the entire city. It was a fuel storage. I was afraid of a possible sabotage and a fire breaking out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender 09041 into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 09041 shall be assigned Exhibit D51. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D51 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like to call up P246.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And while we are waiting for the document to be displayed, let me tell you what it's about. It was issued by the command of the 1st Krajina Corps on the 1st of June, 1992. Is that right? Do you see the document in front of you, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 1st of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the document there is a reference, under 2, to the operations of the 19th Brigade of the 30th Partisan Division. Retaliation was carried out against the inhabitants of Cipuljici village who fled to Kupres. The 1st Battalion of the 19th Partisan Brigade has been formed from the 400 Bugojno refugees. Could you please confirm the abbreviation PR TD?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 19th Battalion of the Partisan Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the 19th Part. Brigade?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- it is the 19th Partisan Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're talking about Serbian refugees here; right? Since the 19th Partisan Brigade was formed, or perhaps those were members of some other ethnicity who formed that brigade?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally I believe that they were Serbs, but I am not sure. We know what happened in Bugojno. There were a lot of problems there, unfortunately, and I believe that those were, indeed, Serbian refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know at the time around Bugojno and Kupres whether there was any fighting going on and who was involved?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around Bugojno and Kupres, besides the army units there were also the Croatian HVO units, the Croatian Defence Council units. The Croatian people had organised themselves in order to protect themselves, and I know that there was some fierce fighting going on both in Bugojno and around Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document has already been admitted so there's no need for me to tender it. And now I would like provide the Colonel with his own statement. I am counting on the Prosecutor to have an unmarked version today as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's go to paragraph 67, please.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before we start discussing this paragraph, let me ask you something else about Bugojno and Kupres. In addition to the HVO units, did you know at the time that around Kupres and Bugojno there were also units of the Croatian army, i.e., the Army of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not around Bugojno; but, yes, around Kupres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let's go back to paragraph 67 in your statement. We're talking about casualties in Kozarac. We already discussed that, but I would like to revisit the issue just briefly. Did you subsequently talk to Colonel Marcetic? Did you discuss the figures, namely, 800 or 80, and how many were actually killed in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not discuss that with Marcetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have an opportunity to see a book about those who went missing from Prijedor municipality? The book could be -- the title of the book could be translated as: "Blameless."

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like to call up P247 in -- in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, this was issued by the 1st Krajina Corps in 1992, on the 27th of May. This is about the armed conflict in Kozarac. According to this report, it started on the 25th of May and ended on the 27th of May, 1992. Did you know what the goal of the military column was, and that military column, on the 25th of May, 1992, was passing through Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I know that a battalion had arrived from Belgrade. They were also headed in that direction. I don't know much about the details of the whole situation. That was staged.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that the first driver, i.e., the person driving the first truck, was killed while the column was moving through Kozarac and that was the reason why the column halted in Kozarac in the first place?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. There were debates, there were reports in the media. However, those were political options, and those political options tried to justify the incident during which over 1200 people were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many wounded were there? You're saying that there were 1200 killed. How many wounded? Do you have that information?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I know that there were a lot, but I don't know the exact figure. I don't want to speculate. Unfortunately, there were a lot of wounded people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you say that there were several thousand wounded, if you say that there were 1200 killed?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. Because the population from the villages around Prijedori was taken to three major camps that contained over 5.000 people. There were a lot of wounded among them who succumbed to their wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In other words, all of those wounded were brought to the camps and they were treated there?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And there should be documents to that effect, about the number of wounded?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That documentation was hidden to mask up the responsibility of the perpetrators. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One after the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's now Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about the losses suffered by the military column? How many killed? How many wounded?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know some were killed. I see from that -- this document, five killed, 20 wounded. They were from the 23rd Motorised Brigade that was based in Prijedor and that perpetrated this crime in Kozarac. It was genocide.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will leave legal terms, such as genocide, for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like you to focus on the facts because you are a fact witness. You are not an expert witness, so please refrain from making evaluations and judgements. Just tell us about your personal knowledge, what you heard at that time or saw at that time. Please. Did you hear about fighting in Hambarine two or three days before the fighting started in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not hear about any actual fighting. There was a debate in the media about all that, but it was all carefully put out and -- and orchestrated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Selak, the question was did you hear about it. You said: "No, I did not hear about any actual fighting." That's an answer to the question instead of then giving your opinion about whether it was orchestrated or not. You are a witness of fact. What you know, tell us. What you observed, tell us. What you think, keep it for yourself if you're not asked about it. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Selak, did you hear about an attack on Prijedor town several days after Kozarac, on the 30th of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I should now like to call up in e-court 1D111.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting, Mr. Lukic, may I take you back to an earlier observation you made this morning. You said that yesterday you had spoken about paragraph 5 of that previous document, of the 14th of April, and I couldn't find that. As a matter of fact, the witness said yesterday something about persons leaving their apartments, not about confiscation, but that was not in the context of any question related to paragraph 5 of this 14th of April document. As a matter of fact, you started with paragraph 1, and that's where we stopped, where the witness had testified about persons leaving their apartments but, again, not in the context of what we read in paragraph 5. That is, movement of, the kind of activity which was not referred to. So I'm a bit confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I thought that I was reading from that paragraph yesterday, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you started reading paragraph 1. But I may have missed it, or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are right. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to you whether you still want to visit the matter or not, but I was confused by your reference to the reading of paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was paragraph 1, Your Honour. My mistake. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I covered today paragraph 5 as well. If you think that I should cover more --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm not -- I just wanted to say that where you referred to what you had done yesterday, that I -- it was my recollection that you had not done that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here on your screen, you can see an order by Colonel Hasan Efendic dated 29 April 1992. We can read in it that Colonel Efendic orders a complete blockade on all roads in Bosnia-Herzegovina where the JNA is beginning to withdrew its equipment and personnel in direct co-ordination with the Ministry of Interior. Item 2 says: Block the broader area of military installations from which attempts are made to pull out equipment using all sorts of natural features and man-made obstacles to prevent the JNA and the MUP from doing that. You told us about this yesterday, but we were discussing, actually, an earlier period in April. After this order, were you able to observe an increased activity in mounting obstacles to movements of military equipment and personnel?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not observe on the territory of the 1st Krajina Corps such a thing, or you did not hear that it happened in areas held by the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I hope you will allow me to explain this in greater detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please first give an answer to the question. The question whether -- was whether you did not observe what was -- what Mr. Lukic told you, or that you did not hear that it happened. Could you first answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it didn't happen. The units were strong enough to protect their assets. I'm asking you to let me explain this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Selak, I said first answer the question. Do I then understand that if you say it didn't happen that you couldn't see it because you can't see anything that doesn't happen. Is that your answer? The short answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was living and working in Banja Luka, and in Bosanska Krajina it did not happen. In other parts of Bosnia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other parts of Bosnia, I believe it did happen because there was an order by the Yugoslav People's Army to pull out all equipment and assets from territories held by Bosniaks because they were afraid the Bosniaks would take that equipment and weapons. If -- you're not letting me answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because you're not answering the question. You said you believe it didn't happen because there was an order. That is conclusions. The question clearly was: Did you see it happen? We've received an answer to that because you said, In the area where I was, it did not happen. Therefore, I could not see it happen. And further away, it may have happened. You have heard about it to happen further away? Did you hear that at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did hear about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, next question. Next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 68 now in your statement, please.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Regarding this paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see P248.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You see here in paragraph 1 of this document: "In the course of the day, the enemy has mostly continued to observe the cease-fire, expect in the area north of Derventa and south of Bosanski Brod where several serious artillery and infantry fire provocations occurred during the day." It was about 26 July 1992. Are you aware - although you were retired at the time - that in these locations, all the way up to the end of July 1992, fighting went on?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Also, in para 3, it says: "The complexity of the social and financial situation, shortages, and cuts in electrical power," et cetera. Do you remember any blackouts and shortages of power in Banja Luka at the time?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it happened occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement, regarding this document, you say -- speaking of Keraterm, you say: "This shows that Keraterm camp was in the area of responsibility of the 1st Krajina Corps because they would not reporting about something outside of their area of responsibility." First of all, I would like to ask you: In which military document is the area of responsibility defined; do you know?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which document, but I know that Banja Luka Corps covered the entire Bosnian Krajina, including Prijedor, with its 343rd Motorised Brigade that was committing crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who provided guards for Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was part of the responsibilities of those who established it, and that was the Banja Luka Corps and the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the source of your information? If can you enlighten us so we can find it too.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a professional colonel and I had colleagues, Serbs, who told me about what was going on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you ever seen any document about it? Everything is written up in the army. Have you ever seen a document saying that the Keraterm camp was established by the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember seeing the document. I might have. But I don't remember any details. I can't answer this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, everything that is written up in the army is comment, not part of a question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Colonel, that there should be - there must be - a written trace in the archives of the 1st Krajina Corps, if they, indeed, established Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, some of those reports were false, such as the report involving 80 men, because they were afraid of the legal consequences, knowing that that action was illegal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Selak, that was not the question. The question was whether there must be a written trace, which is conclusion or opinion you're asking for, Mr. Lukic, at this moment. Why you emphasised a minute ago that this is a witness of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I withdraw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness knows anything about it, he can tell us; if not, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you ever supply Keraterm with anything? Did you send food there or anything else?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Keraterm was also in your zone, wasn't it? The zone that you used to supply.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Keraterm. The entire Bosnian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Including Prijedor where it was based?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That brigade was also Prijedor, and I sent supplies to the brigade as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not at the same time. Pause between question and answer and between answer and question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Bear with me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Selak, if Mr. Lukic asks you, Keraterm was also in your zone, the zone that you used to supply. You said: "Not Keraterm. The entire Bosnian Krajina." You have not carefully listened to the question. The question was not whether Keraterm was the zone but whether Keraterm was in the zone. So the simple answer would have been: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please. Please, just a few words. The logistical base does not supply directly the lowest subordinate units. It supplies the corps and its units, whereas Keraterm was not a corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But I didn't invite you to make further explanations. The location where Keraterm was was within the zone you supplied by the means as you have explained to us before, not directly but through the corps. You have told us that already. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you tell us where your depots were, where was your quartermaster depot, where was your ammunition depot, the depot of medical supplies?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the logistical base in Banja Luka had ammunition depots in Mrkonjic Grad, Donji Vakuf, and in Banja Luka. Fuel depots in Jajce and in Banja Luka. A depot of spare parts and quartermaster's equipment in Banja Luka. That's my answer. And that includes medical supplies and everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You provided comment on 18347. It is an order of Lieutenant-Colonel Momir Talic dated 7 June 1993, it says here. It deals with the preparation of sectors for HVO prisoners of war at Manjaca. Did you see this document during proofing?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, this is the setting up of the centre for the detention of prisoners of war in 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it the army's obligation to set up centres, or camps, where they would keep prisoners of war? What was the way prisoners of war were kept?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army is responsible for the safety and security of POWs, so Camp Manjaca was within the military and it's only logical that the army should be responsible for the camp and take care of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us please focus on paragraph 69 now of your statement. If you remember, in this document you discussed in great deal with my colleague, Mr. Ackerman -- actually, you gave your comment on document 03847. I'm not going to be calling it up. We don't need it in e-court. But you say that the corps issued weapons to the units of the Territorial Defence from the very beginning of operations with the intention of protecting Serbs in the Serb republic from genocide, that is, where there is a table with a detailed explanation of the equipment issued to the Territorial Defence units. Can we agree that at that time the Serbs in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina did not have their own army; is that right? They were only involved in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Your Honours, on the 18th of May, 1992, the units were renamed into the Army of Republika Srpska. The JNA units. So yes, they did have their army. It was officially the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Just a moment, please. Survey --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let us call up 3847 in e-court after all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, reference to what was discussed with Mr. Ackerman, of course, the Chamber is not privy of that because it's not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You see the document. This is a report of the Command of the 1st Krajina Corps dated the 31st of August, 1992. But we need page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, could you please zoom in on the left part of the document. But first the top of the page, I'm sorry. Could we also have the top of the page in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The heading is: "Survey of Weapons and Equipment Issued to Staffs and Units of the TO from the 5th Corps." The 5th Corps existed before the 18th of May, 1992; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 5th Corps of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was renamed and became the 1st Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska on the 18th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So when it is written here that this is a document of the 5th Corps, the time concerned is before the 18th of May. So now I'm going to ask you a question. And you were actually asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document is weapons and equipment issued to TO staffs and units of the 5th Corps. So let me just try to fully understand what you just said. The time concerned is before the 15th of May -- yes, at least as far as the 5th Corps is concerned. Yes, please proceed. I'm trying to follow. And now and then, if I'm a bit slow, Mr. Lukic, I hope you will for give me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is a bit confusing because it was merge of two documents, actually. One is from the 1st [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That may have --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- Corps and the other one is from the 5th Corps of JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But it also includes the TO?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I'm trying to find ... I'm trying to find -- I will be able to find it later on. I know that I have it. The transcript from Brdjanin trial. And is it appropriate time for the break, Your Honour. It will help me organise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you would have time to find the sources you would like to use. It's a good time for a break. We take a break after the witness has been escorted out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, Mr. Selak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, consultations, please, at a volume that it doesn't -- is not heard by others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And preferably during the break. Yes, we received some hard --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was saved by the bell --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you were [Overlapping speakers] ... yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- at the end of the last session, so I discovered, actually, I don't have this excerpt from the transcript and it's not in the system, actually. So I provided Your Honours with a written part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll try then to get this moment on the basis of the hard copy provided to us. It's always good to be saved, Mr. Lukic. Can the witness be brought into the courtroom. And, meanwhile, I address the parties on filing deadlines. The Chamber noticed that the Defence has been relying for some time on the distribution date of a motion as the trigger date for when a response is to be filed. The Chamber understands that the Defence may have relied on Article 25, paragraph 4, of the directive for the Court Management and Support Services Section, judicial support services, IT 121, ref. 2. The Chamber, irrespective of its views whether Article 25 of this directive could overrule Rule 126 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, wishes to clarify that it orders the parties to abide by Rule 126 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber draws the Defence's attention to the Appeals Chamber's case law on this issue two decisions in the Gotovina case of - a decision, the first one - of the 17th of January, 2008, in paragraph 22; and a decision of the 3rd of April, 2012, footnote 8, and expects that the parties comply with deadlines in accordance with this case law which is oriented towards the day of filing rather than the time of distribution. In case of a substantial difference between the day of filing and the time of distribution, parties may request an extension of the deadline. Mr. Selak, it's not very polite to continue talking when you enter the courtroom. Apologies for that. We'll now continue with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Colonel, we may go on.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have an excerpt here from a transcript, from the 21st of January, 2003. That is when you discussed this topic with Mr. Ackerman, the one that we'll be discussing now. There's no point in giving you the English version -- or would you like to have the English version?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's why I'm going to read this out. 13214 is the page reference. The transcript of the Brdjanin trial. The 21st of January, 2003. I would like to start with line 13. You are actually discussing this table that we have before us now on our screens, and this is what Mr. Ackerman, my colleague, says: "Now, looking again at this document, and bearing in mind that there was war going on in Croatia between Croatian military forces and the JNA, let's just look at each one of these entries here." And then he asks you about the locations listed in this table. He asks you whether Okucani is in Croatia, and you say yes. Then Prnjavor is located close to the Croatian border region. And you say it is not the border region. There is Bosanska Gradiska between them. And then Ackerman says: "What is it, 30 kilometres?" And you say: "That order of magnitude but I'm not sure." Do you remember all of this, witness?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I remember the testimony but I don't remember that particular information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. He asked you about Petrinja, whether it's in Croatia and you said yes. Would you agree with that today as well?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Krupa is at the border, and you say not quite on the border. It's close.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Omarska, and you say Omarska isn't either. It's in Bosnia. And then -- actually, can you tell us today - part of the text is missing here - how far away from the border is Omarska?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Omarska, since it's by Prijedor, it's about 35 to 40 kilometres, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sanski Most? How far away is it from the border, roughly?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sanski Most is a bit closer. I think it's 25 to 30. I was in Sanski Most several times, but I never went to Croatia from there. However, looking at the map it would be 25 to 30 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Bosanska Gradiska is on the border; right?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's divided by the Sava river.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Banja Luka, you say it's 50-odd kilometres.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the closest in terms of Bosanska Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then there's a reference to Western Slavonia. That's in Croatia; right?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Bosanski Novi, it's on the border; right?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ackerman is taking you through all of these calibres for automatic rifles, and he is telling you where these weapons ended up. We actually have that on the table in front of us. And then, finally, my colleague, Mr. Ackerman, asks you the following. He says, on page 13216, line 20, Mr. Ackerman says: "Sir, when we analyse -- when you analyse this document, and when you see where these weapons went, a vast majority went either to the border with Croatia, where there was a war going on or to Croatia."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The reference is not right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Interpreters draw our attention to the fact that the reference is not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it seems that the reference is not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It seems so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please find the place of the quote and otherwise take your time and do it at a later moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will not need the reference to put the question to the colonel. We will include the reference subsequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it seems to be on page 13215, line 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we passed that, Your Honour. It's obviously some page which is missing at the end. But thank you for your help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I repeat the page number. It's not recorded correctly. It's 13215.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Indiscernible]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now it's corrected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you proceed, we'll also try to assist you in finding it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman asked you as follows: "It was not about the arming of civilians in the middle of Republika Srpska. This document, in essence, shows that there was an ongoing effort to respond to the war in Croatia and to arm those forces who fought over there; is that correct?" And to that question, you answered yes. Your answer is on page 13217. If you were asked the same thing again today, would you agree that this is what the document shows, that the forces were being armed on the border and in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it applied only to the Serbian people. This is what I would adhere to. Only the Serbian people was being armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the Croatian front line ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, your mike.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if that would assist you, the quote you were trying to find is on page 13218, and I'm going on to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- 9. It starts, indeed, at line 20. If you want me to read it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then I will try to do that slowly so as to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was the following by Mr. Ackerman: "Q. Now, sir, when you analyse this document as to where these weapons were going, the vast majority of them were going either on the border area next to Croatia, where the war was, or in Croatia. And rather than some scheme that got dreamed up by someone that this was an effort to arm civilians in the middle of Republika Srpska, the document basically shows that it was an effort to deal with the war going on in Croatia and arm the units that were fighting there, doesn't it?" Do you want me to read the answer as well, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you answered -- you said -- and it's a pretty long answer, Mr. Lukic, so tell me when you want me to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would stop after yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would stop after yes. Yes, but ... Your answer was the following: "Yes. But it also means that the objective, the purpose of this was to protect the Serbian people, as it was said officially, to protect the Serbian people in the area of the Republic of Croatia, and that's the reason why these units remained there. And I repeat: The UN forces controlled these weapons which had to be stored in warehouses. I don't know what happened later. I never visited the area after that. Whether truly the tanks and the guns were in the warehouses or not, I don't know, but I know that they were handed over. You have the document here and the date, but as to the relevant quantities, and if and whether this went to private homes, I don't think so. That was the TO, the local units. I'm not saying paramilitary units because, after all, it was the army that exerted control over these weapons. I mean, if they had issued, handed over the weapons, then they must have had some kind of control over these weapons in order to prevent any abuse." That was the full answer, Mr. Lukic. Now, if -- if I'm able to find it within one minute and a half, then I think that perhaps the other members of the team could do the same. And it's easy. You go to the relevant transcript, you search for the word "analyse," and you have it within one minute. But let me not interrupt the flow of evidence any further. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your help, Your Honour. And I have to try to excuse my -- members of our team, since they are doing something else and I was just trying during the break to cover what I missed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But it was basically my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you provide the same answer today as you did to Mr. Ackerman? However, I would like to add something to that, Your Honours. The corps was not authorised to supply the illicit -- it would -- should have been done by the logistics base, but this went behind the back of the logistics base because the corps should not have over 5 per cent more weapons for his own contingent. Where did they get all those weapons from? Actually that was a question for you, because this was within your purview.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I understand that. The units were withdrawing from Croatia, the corps took weapons, they didn't identify it, they did not first hand it over to the base, but they distributed it by bypassing the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So that would be your answer?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In Croatia, in the war-affected area, there were no Bosniaks in practical terms. There were only Serbs and Croats there.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time, Croats attacked the units and facilities of the JNA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were asked previously, and I'm going to repeat that question, is it only logical that the JNA would provide weapons to those who were not attacking them rather to those who were attacking them? Does it make any sense?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croatia had a referendum in which it proclaimed independence and the JNA units were supposed to withdraw from the territory of Croatia. Therefore, they were the occupying army in the area and it was only normal to fight to liberate one's own territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your explanation. However, you did not provide an answer to my question.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did give you my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, okay. We see on this list - I don't know whether you can see it or not - there is a device called curve metre. What is curve metre?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an instrument which measures distances in kilometres on topographic maps, to provide the officer with the exact distance between his units. According to a topographic map, a curve metre is adjusted to be able to measure distances between various points.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who you gave it to? Because it says others.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember. I -- this really surprises me because I really don't know that I ever gave it to somebody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, as far as I'm familiar with what a curve metre is, the special feature of it is - and that is different from just measuring distances - is that you can follow routes, roads, there's a little wheel on it, you follow it, and then it measures the distance as if you had been driven over that road. That's my understanding of what a curve metre is. "Curve" standing for "curves," which is not linear distance but through roads. I just raise this so that we have full understanding of what a curve metre really is. If -- unless there's any disagreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: With this regard, you say in the same paragraph, the first note is dated 26 December 1991. I would like to draw your attention to paragraph 8 entitled: "General Vidovic, Assistant for Political Education." And on page 6 it says: "The full recognition of Croatia and Slovenia will not materialise so soon. The United Nations have to give their approval first. B and H will stay with Yugoslavia. The Serbian Republic of Krajina will be part of a new Yugoslavia." My question: At that time, B and H was part of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time, it was still the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Why were you shocked at the time by the fact that the officer of the federal army was defending the state that he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you share the same view on that issue at the time, or was your view different?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the republics held a referendum --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Selak. We're talking about the 26th December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I attended that meeting, and in my Official Note that I have on me, I recorded that, precisely that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you: Was it a normal way of thinking on the part of an officer of the JNA on the 26th of December, 1991, or was that something unusual? Why did you take a note of that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a normal way of thinking because the political situation in Yugoslavia changed by the day and people started opting for different solutions and different options when it comes to the destiny of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: However, you say that the remarks originate from General Vukovic, the commander of the 5th Corps who, on the 28th of December, 1991, i.e., two days after the -- this was note, took over from Uzelac, "I was very concerned about Vukovic's remarks." Why did you find this a matter of concern?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I knew that the JNA would resist Croatia and Slovenia that wanted to organise themselves as independent state. My fear came true, there was fighting and thousands of people were dead. It is better to negotiate for 100 years than to wage a war for a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, we agree on that. You say further on that the armoured battalion from Pancevo headed for Kupres and Plitvice lakes. At that time, was that illegal in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not illegal or unlawful. However, there were battalions in the 7th Army District. But Banja Luka had an armoured battalion. Why didn't the Banja Luka Brigade send its own armoured battalion? Why did it have to arrive from Pancevo? That was my concern. And that pointed to the growing problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Colonel, how long was the front line that was held by the 1st Krajina Corps which was, at that time, the 5th Banja Luka Corps?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their zone of responsibility was vast but it was still peacetime and the brigade had 101 tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the line that was covered by the 5th Corps, as it was known at that time, the front line was over 1200 kilometres long?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The line of the zone of responsibility of the corps was big, but the line itself was not as long as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long was it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. Please, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking if you know. If you don't, it's your legitimate right to say no.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't want to provide an incorrect answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's go to paragraph 80 in your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, one of the answers of the witness was that it was still peacetime and you asked him about the front lines. I have some difficulties in reconciling front lines with peace. You were talking about front lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not the witness. Do you consider that it was war already?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... clarified partially, but I can go back to that issue, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at least I noticed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Selak, indeed, there is some collision here and I think that both you and I understand it but we need to clarify it for everyone else. The front line existed in Croatia; right?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Eastern Slavonia, down there towards the border with Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when you say that it was peacetime, you are referring to a part of Bosnia-Herzegovina that was covered by the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in paragraph 80, you say: "The next important entry is dated the 24th of February, 1992 ... the Serb municipality of Donji Vakuf had been proclaimed." Then you say: "This could only have been proclaimed because a garrison was stationed in Donji Vakuf and this garrison was part of the 30th Division under the command of Colonel Galic."

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stanislav, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Donji Vakuf had a Serb minority but they were able to claim it as a Serbian municipality due to military support." Would you agree with me that at this point in time there weren't any conflicts? There weren't any conflicts in the territory of the municipality of Donji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was that a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Were there any conflicts in Donji Vakuf in February 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the municipality of Donji Vakuf, there was a large arms depot within my -- well, I'm saying this conditionally, my logistics base that I commanded. And the 30th Partisan Division that was at Mrkonjic Grad also covered Donji Vakuf. There weren't any combat operations going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This decision to declare a municipality is a political decision and it is the will of certain political parties. It's not the result of combat.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the army had nothing to do with this kind of declaration or proclamation?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well it shouldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Pause, Mr. Lukic. Yes, please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no cause for concern because there weren't any combat operations. Now why the Serb people decided to do this, I don't understand. But we see what happened later. Already in May 1992, they blew up the bridge across the Vrbas river, and you could not get to the arms depot in Donji Vakuf and go towards Bugojno. There was no bridge to be crossed, if you take a truck. That's my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This municipality that had been proclaimed, it did not encompass the entire of the territory of the municipality of Donji Vakuf; right? Only parts of it.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the municipality of Donji Vakuf there was a Serb population of about 34 per cent, 60 per cent were Muslims and about 45 -- 4 to 5 per cent were Croats. So they proclaimed a municipality there. I mean, they could have their government in the area where the Serbs were only, not throughout the territory of the municipality of Donji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now briefly concerning paragraph 84. In this paragraph, you say: "In my diary I have an entry for 4th June 1992 from a briefing at General Djukic's, assistant for logistics on the staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, B and H, who said: The federal government will finance that army, including all persons employed as of 19 May 1992 who had previously been on the federal payroll." My question focuses on the following sentence: "In my view," you go on to say, "this comment by General Djukic shows that the Serbian army in Bosnia-Herzegovina was working for Yugoslavia, considering that the Yugoslav federal government was paying for it." We can also see it on the screen. It's Exhibit 1277. That's an excerpt from the transcript in Dusko Tadic case on 5th June 1996, page 1227 [as interpreted], lines 17 through 24. You were asked whether there was a command structure between the Army of Yugoslavia and the Army of Republika Srpska, at that time the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and you said there was no real command structure. How would you testify today, was there a command structure between the JNA and the Bosnian Serbs army or not?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no direct command responsibility, Your Honours. However, in Belgrade, the 30th Personnel Centre was established to deal precisely with the problems and issues of the Serbian army in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and all the active-duty officers of the JNA who remained in Bosnia and Herzegovina received their salaries and retirement pensions from Belgrade. I was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. That was explained extensively enough before this Tribunal. But I would now like to come back to paragraph 65 in your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if something is sufficiently explained before this Tribunal, it doesn't mean that it's in evidence before this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. Just one second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your statement, paragraph 65 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you continue, you referred to the -- was that the Tadic? Yes. "That's an excerpt from the transcript in Dusko Tadic case on the 5th of June, 1996, page 1227, lines 17 through 24."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That doesn't resolve my problem. Because as far as I am aware of, the 5th of June, 1996, morning session, starts with page 1838, so I have difficulties in -- now, I could have a look on whether, what you referred to -- let me just try to see whether the text can be found on that day. If not ... I don't find anything. You did not give a literal quote. But at least we cannot find this in the source, as you indicated it. And I rely - and perhaps I shouldn't do that - on the Internet transcript as found on the ICTY web site because that's not an official source. At the same time, I -- when you have shown to have difficulties in coming to the right source, I use this informal source both to assist and now to challenge, to some extent, your reference to the source.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for assisting. I'll try to respond correctly after the break on this challenge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In paragraph 65: That document conveys the official position of the corps command to all members of the corps. The position expressed in that document is the reason why I left the army. And that was an information report on the situation on the ground dated 11 April 1992. So I would like us to see on the screen 18348 in e-court. We have already agreed that the policy of the JNA was to preserve Yugoslavia as a whole and not to allow its breakup along ethnic lines, along republic borders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. I have problems today with transcripts from other cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 13194 from the Brdjanin trial, you were asked the question by Mr. Ackerman, and you confirmed in lines 20 to 25, we see the question and answer. You confirmed: "Would you agree today that the Yugoslav army was trying not to allow Yugoslavia break up along ethnic lines?"

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was its duty to protect the entire territory of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the SFRY. That was its reason for existence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the date of that transcript, Mr. Lukic, which you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The date is, Your Honour, 20th of January, 2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask Mr. Lukic to actually read the passage. I believe what he has paraphrased is somewhat different.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that, Your Honour, so Colonel can get a proper translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman asks you: [In English] It's correct - isn't it? - that the official policy of the JNA was to keep Yugoslavia together and oppose the ethnic breakup of Yugoslavia. And your answer on the line 25 was: "Yes." [Interpretation] You answered that question yes. Would you answer yes today to the same question?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, with one proviso. The composition of the officer cadre of the Yugoslav army at that time was 60-something per cent, Serbs and Montenegrins, and only 30 per cent were Croats, Macedonians, and others. It was quite clear at that time who was dominating the Yugoslav army, and they wanted domination over the whole territory of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to this report, one of the sentences is: "The greatest suffering is in Kupres where fierce fighting is taking place between the armed formations of Croatia and the Serbian people from these areas. The objective of the Croatian state's diabolical plans is to take Kupres (regardless of casualties) and to join up the BH HDZ paramilitaries along the Bugojno-Doboj-Bosanski Brod axis." Do you know that there were HVO forces around Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And they had been established by the Croatian population from Bugojno and from around Bugojno against Kupres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would connecting this transversal Bugojno, Kupres, Bosanski Brod, would the uniting of HOS and ZNG units, both of them Croatian, cut off the Bosnian Krajina and the Croatian Krajina from the rest of the territories held at that time by the Serbs and from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Croatia committed aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina precisely in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is mentioned here that 28 people were killed by having their throats slit. Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. It was a long time ago. I can't answer that question. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you recall it if I told you there was a crime in the villages of Donji and Gornji Malovan?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, General Mladic was there but it was in Bihac when Bihac was about to fall before the Serbian forces. Yes, that's when you were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic should not intervene during the examination of the witness. But no such question was asked, was it? Mr. Lukic? Or did I miss anything? Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, there was no question. There was no question in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you refrain from spontaneously telling us matters you think are relevant but are not part of the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He provoked me, Your Honour. General Mladic did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Mr. Mladic addressed the witness at that time, then one more word in the presence of the witness, which addresses him, Mr. Mladic, and that is considered to be inappropriate behaviour, which may lead to being removed from the courtroom. So I would urge you to refrain from ever doing it again. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may explain, Your Honour, how I understood. The words from Mr. Mladic were addressed to me just telling me the names of two villages I repeated to this witness. So I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic, I have urged again and again that if Mr. Mladic wants to consult with you, he should do it at low voice so as not to be heard by anyone else, and now we see the results that -- what happens if he doesn't do that. And during breaks, Mr. Mladic, you always can provide further information or can you provide it to Mr. Stojanovic if at a low voice, not to be heard by other persons in this courtroom. You can -- you may remain seated, Mr. Mladic. No reason to stand. And please switch off your microphone. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this same document towards the bottom of the page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Low voice, I said, Mr. Mladic. And Mr. Lukic -- I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic is just repeated that he didn't address Colonel Selak and that he was just addressing me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is no need to do that. You have told us and I have explained that this is the result of not following the instructions he has received on consulting with counsel. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you see towards the bottom of the page, fourth line from below: "Fire was opened at military installations mostly from infantry weapons but also from artillery weapons." Do you know how come the attacking forces had artillery?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we have to find our source. We can choose from 30 lines and are unable to immediately spot it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you give me one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The problem is that paragraphs are different in the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Just after the words "in open parliament" in quotations marks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's on the first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 15 rows from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. And also from the interpreters who are actively following.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question was this: Do you know where did the forces attacking JNA got their artillery weapons from?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Didn't have any artillery weapons. This is a piece of false information. They had rifles and sniping rifles. I know that. But they didn't have any artillery. They didn't have the -- that because the police and the military organisation would have confiscated those. This is false. This is a lie. This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time were some military depots already taken over?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the city of Sarajevo, some were. I don't know about the general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you don't know how the attacking forces were armed in the first place?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were fuel storages and quartermasters' depots. There were no ammunition depots in the city, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Who launched those attacks?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Groups that were organised and that were in favour of the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina from Yugoslavia. That was the initial fight for independence, because the army covered the republic and did not allow any activities to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. On page 2 -- I'm looking for page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you seek clarification as to the source of knowledge, especially of the last answer. Who the attacks launched, how do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my colleagues lived in Sarajevo. Other officers, my brothers, sisters, my relatives, they all lived there and I received the exact information as to what was going on in Sarajevo because I communicated with my colleagues and brothers and sisters on a daily basis, and that's where I got my information from and I adhere about what I learnt from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were they themselves involved in these attacks or was it hearsay for them as well?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask them where the information was from. However, my nephew, unfortunately, got killed during those activities. He was killed by the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic. For a couple of minutes and then we take a break. Unless this would be a suitable moment for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can break here, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. Mr. Selak, we take a break. Would you please follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, your on your feet. Are you preparing to start the break or is there another reason?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I was just going to say that I do have some additional information with respect to the topic that was discussed this morning that I would like to say at some point today, but I'll leave it to the Chamber to decide when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it about the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, we were waiting for written submissions. Now if you could share your information with Mr. Lukic and see whether that brings you any step further.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, there has been a suggestion that the Prosecution hasn't fulfilled its Rule 68 obligation, and I never like to leave that unspoken or unclarified for too long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would tell us when you disclosed the information, the statement of the author. Is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In essence, Your Honour, pursuant to the Chamber's direction yesterday to investigate the matter further we identified this statement. Upon checking with our disclosure log for this particular case, we could not find an entry for it so we disclosed it immediately. This morning while -- we did that before we checked the records of the general EDS collection.
